text:
Anna (CS): MosaicMed onboarding — AP-SOUTH pilot tomorrow. They hit throttles in staging during load test. Need temporary QPS bump + CIDR allowlist to cover demo. Renewal in ~6 weeks; high churn risk if demo flakes. Request: raise org qps from 120 -> 800, apply CIDRs 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/26, start 2026-03-24T03:00Z, desired duration 48h, autorevoke at 72h. Can someone review and coordinate infra + security? :pray:

Jordan (SE): Got it. What's their org id and expected call pattern? Are these sustained or short bursts?

Anna (CS): org_mosaicmed_42. Calls are short chat completions, avg length ~256 tokens. Baseline steady ~120 RPS, demo can spike to ~800 RPS for ~20-40 minutes bursts. Most traffic will originate from a single cloud region (ap-south-1) via a small set of egress IPs.

Mike (NetOps): I can handle the CIDR add and the rate rule, but I need a support ticket with justification + start/end times and the exact CIDRs again. Also confirm whether we'll route them to ap-south-only or allow multi-region failover.

Anna (CS): Confirm AP-SOUTH only for the pilot. Start 2026-03-24T03:00Z, end 2026-03-26T03:00Z, autorevoke at 2026-03-27T03:00Z (72h). CIDRs: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/26. I'll open the ticket and include renewal risk note.

Sophie (Security): Quick security check — MosaicMed is hosted (not private deploy), correct? If so, we prefer header-based allowlisting + signed HMAC header for safety rather than broad CIDR opens. Do they have static egress IPs that are guaranteed? We need to avoid opening our edge wide.

Anna (CS): They confirmed static egress IPs from their cloud provider and provided the CIDRs above. They can also sign a custom X-Company-Signature header if we want HMAC. They prefer hosted API for speed.

Jordan (SE): Plan: create a canary route for org_mosaicmed_42 with a soft limit at 800 qps and aggressive monitoring for 30 mins, then promote. I'll drop a test snippet here.

Jordan (SE): ```bash
# quick smoke test against canary route
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "X-Company-Signature: sha256=..." \
  -H "X-Org-Id: org_mosaicmed_42" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"healthcheck"}'
```

Mike (NetOps): I'll open the infra ticket now and add the CIDRs to the ap-south allowlist. Will configure a temporary rate policy for org_mosaicmed_42 -> qps=800 window=48h and set an autorevoke job at 72h. Creating ticket: INC-5428. Linking in a sec.

Mike (NetOps): INC-5428 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-5428 — description: MosaicMed AP-SOUTH pilot temporary QPS bump + CIDR allowlist. Assigned to netops-team. ETA for rule apply: 20 min.

Sophie (Security): Thanks. Please ensure the HMAC header check is optional but recommended; add a note that if we see anomalous traffic patterns we escalate and reduce the soft limit. Also add monitoring alert: 5xx rate >0.5% OR latency p95 > 1.0s -> paging.

Anna (CS): Added renewal-risk flag to the ticket and pinged the AM for a renewal health check meeting. Also requested customer provide signed HMAC token before the pilot start. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Rate limit policy queued: org=org_mosaicmed_42 qps=800 duration=48h autorevoke=72h allowlist=[203.0.113.0/24,198.51.100.0/26] region=ap-south-1

Mike (NetOps): Rules applied to edge in ap-south-1. INC-5428 updated with change log. Please monitor canary and confirm with Jordan when you see stable behaviour.

Jordan (SE): Canary healthy after 25m. No 5xx, p95 latency ~0.45s. Promoting to soft-prod route and will keep the 800qps cap for the window.

Anna (CS): Awesome — I'll run the demo with the customer tomorrow and monitor. Leaving renewal risk note: high-touch required, follow-up meeting scheduled for 2026-04-05. Thanks team! :party:
